meta.titre: Map Reading and Interpretation: answering 'with map evidence only' questions on relief, drainage and settlement

sections.contenu_markdown: Paper 3 often gives a topographic map of a highland area of the North West Region, such as the sheets built around Bamenda and Santa in recent papers. Towns there are squeezed between steep slopes, streams and forest, so examiners ask what the map shows, why settlement is thick in one place and thin in another, and what could be done to let a town grow. The instruction "with map evidence only" is the key: marks go to statements that can be checked on the sheet, never to general knowledge about the region. This course teaches you to read the sheet quickly and to turn each observation into a full mark.

items: A contour is a line joining points of equal height above sea level, and the contour interval is the height difference between two neighbouring contours.
On a topographic map, north is at the top unless the sheet says otherwise, and the key explains every symbol.
A grid reference gives the easting (the vertical line number) first and the northing (the horizontal line number) second.

sections.titre: Reading a topographic map and building answers from map evidence
sections.contenu_markdown:
### The rule for every mark: point, evidence, effect
A "with map evidence only" question rewards statements that can be checked on the sheet. Give (1) the point, (2) the evidence (a grid reference, a spot height, a contour value, a named feature or a symbol from the key) and, when the question speaks of a constraint, a difficulty or a reason, (3) the effect on people. Outside knowledge earns nothing.

### What to read on the map
| Feature | Read from the map | Useful words |
|---|---|---|
| Relief | spot heights, contour values, spacing of contours, direction of slope | steep where contours are close together, gentle where they are far apart, valley, spur, escarpment, plateau, col |
| Drainage | blue lines, flow direction (from high to low ground), tributaries, confluences, swamp symbols, broken lines for seasonal streams | dendritic, parallel or radial pattern, high or low density, perennial, seasonal, meander, flood plain |
| Settlement | built-up areas, villages, scattered buildings, road junctions | nucleated, linear or dispersed; dense or scanty |
| Communications | classes of road, tracks, bridges, footpaths | all-weather road, junction, bridging point |
| Land cover | forest, plantation, swamp, farmland symbols | reserve, cultivated land, waterlogged ground |

### From description to explanation
**Relief as a constraint.** Steep slopes and closely spaced contours make building plots costly to level, roads costly to build and houses liable to landslides. Deep valleys cut the land into separate pieces, and high ground is far from the centre and hard to serve with water and electricity.

**Drainage as a constraint.** Swampy valley floors and flood plains are unsafe for building. Many streams force the building of bridges and culverts, which raises the cost of roads.

**Scanty settlement.** Reasons that a map can support are steep ground, swamp, forest or reserve land, and the absence of roads and services.

**Functions of a town.** Use symbols: offices suggest an administrative function, markets and shops a commercial one, schools an educational one, hospitals a health one, churches or mosques a religious one, and a road junction a transport one.

### Measures that match the problem
For steep relief: terracing, cut-and-fill levelling, roads that follow the contours or zigzag up the slope, and growth towards gentler ground. For poor drainage: drainage channels, embankments, raised building platforms, bridges and culverts, and reclamation of swamps where it is environmentally acceptable.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the command word is describe, state or identify.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Give as many separate, evidenced points as there are marks. A four-mark question needs four different facts, each with a height, a grid reference or a named feature. Write short complete sentences and avoid explanations, which are not asked for.

variantes.nom: Suggest, show how and reasons questions
variantes.quand_utiliser: When you must link a feature to a problem or propose a solution.
variantes.contenu_markdown: State the feature with its evidence, then add the consequence for settlement or development. For a measure, name the problem first and choose a measure that answers it: terracing answers steep slopes, an embankment answers flooding. A measure that does not fit the problem you identified earns no mark.

sections.enonce_markdown:
A fictitious map extract of Town M is drawn at 1:50,000 with a contour interval of 20 m. Town M stands at about 1,200 m in the west of the sheet and one tarred road leaves it towards the west. East of the town the ground rises to a spot height of 1,600 m, and the horizontal distance on the map between the 1,200 m contour and the 1,600 m contour is 4 cm.

With map evidence only: (a) describe the relief east of Town M (3 marks); (b) show how it limits the growth of the town eastwards (2 marks); (c) calculate the average gradient between the two contours (2 marks); (d) suggest one measure to overcome the problem (1 mark).

etapes.action: Read the marks and the command words.
etapes.justification: Describe asks for facts with evidence, show how asks for a link to the town, calculate asks for formula and units, and suggest asks for a measure that fits.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Plan: three evidenced points for (a), cause and effect for (b), a worked gradient for (c), one matching measure for (d).

etapes.action: Describe the relief using heights and spacing.
etapes.justification: Every point must carry numbers from the map. The spacing of contours is found by dividing the map distance by the number of intervals.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The land rises eastwards from about 1,200 m at the town to a spot height of 1,600 m, a rise of 400 m. This is 20 contour intervals of 20 m in 4 cm, so the contours are only about 2 mm apart, which shows a steep slope. The ground is therefore much higher in the east than in the west.

etapes.action: Link the relief to the growth of the town.
etapes.justification: The question asks how relief limits expansion, so each fact needs a consequence.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Steep ground east of the town is costly to level for houses and roads, and landslides are a risk, so the built-up area cannot spread eastwards and must stay on the gentler land in the west.

etapes.justification: Gradient is vertical interval divided by horizontal distance, in the same unit. First convert the map distance to ground distance.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Horizontal distance $=4\times 50\,000=200\,000$ cm $=2\,000$ m. Vertical interval $=1\,600-1\,200=400$ m. Gradient $=\dfrac{400}{2\,000}=\dfrac{1}{5}$, written 1 in 5.

etapes.action: Suggest one measure that answers the problem.
etapes.justification: The problem is steepness, so the measure must reduce the cost or risk of building on slopes.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Cut terraces into the slope and build roads that zigzag up it, or direct growth along the gentler land beside the western road.

sections.conclusion_markdown: Model answer: (a) The land rises from about 1,200 m at Town M to 1,600 m in the east; contours are about 2 mm apart, so slopes are steep; the east is much higher than the west. (b) Steep ground is costly to level and prone to landslides, so the town cannot expand eastwards. (c) The average gradient is **1 in 5**. (d) Terracing the slope, or channelling growth along the gentler western land, would overcome the problem.

items.erreur_markdown: Using outside knowledge: "Bamenda is cool because it is on a high plateau and has volcanic soils".
items.pourquoi_faux: A 'with map evidence only' question gives no credit for facts that the sheet does not show. Climate and soils are not printed on a topographic map.
items.correction_markdown: Quote the sheet: "the spot height of 1,600 m and the closely spaced contours east of the town show high, steep ground".

items.erreur_markdown: Describing relief vaguely: "the land is hilly and the town is on low land".
items.pourquoi_faux: Without heights, contour spacing or a grid reference the examiner cannot verify the statement, so it earns little or nothing.
items.correction_markdown: Give figures: "the town lies at about 1,200 m while the land rises to 1,600 m in the east, with contours about 2 mm apart".

items.erreur_markdown: Saying that closely spaced contours show a gentle slope.
items.pourquoi_faux: Contours close together mean that a large height change happens over a short horizontal distance, which is a steep slope.
items.correction_markdown: Close contours mean steep ground; widely spaced contours mean gentle ground; a gap with no contours means almost flat land.

items.erreur_markdown: Giving a grid reference with the northing before the easting.
items.pourquoi_faux: A grid reference is read along the corridor before up the stairs: easting first, then northing. Reversing the digits places the feature in a different square.
items.correction_markdown: Read the vertical line number on the bottom edge first, then the horizontal line number on the side edge.

items.erreur_markdown: Suggesting "build more schools" as a measure to overcome the difficulties caused by steep relief.
items.pourquoi_faux: The measure does not answer the problem identified. A suggestion must deal directly with the constraint named in the earlier part.
items.correction_markdown: Name a measure that reduces the effect of slope, for example terracing, cut-and-fill levelling or zigzag roads.

items.enonce_markdown: A topographic map is drawn at 1:50,000. (a) Two villages are 6.4 cm apart on the map. How far apart are they on the ground, in kilometres? (b) A road is 4.5 km long on the ground. How long is it on the map, in centimetres? (c) A line of buildings stands along both sides of a single road. Name the settlement pattern.
items.solution_markdown: (a) 1 cm represents 0.5 km, so $6.4\times 0.5=3.2$ km. The villages are **3.2 km** apart. (b) $4.5\div 0.5=9$, so the road is **9 cm** long on the map. (c) Buildings strung along a road form a **linear** settlement.

items.enonce_markdown: A fictitious extract shows these features. A river rises in the north-west and flows south-east, collecting five short streams that join it from both sides at different points. Drawn with solid blue lines, the streams are spread evenly over the whole sheet. Swamp symbols cover the river floor in the south-east, and two broken blue lines in the north end in sand symbols. Describe the drainage characteristics of the extract (4 marks).
items.solution_markdown: Award a mark for each evidenced point, up to four: (1) one main river flows from the north-west to the south-east, so the general slope of the land is towards the south-east; (2) five tributaries join it from both sides, giving a branching, tree-like (dendritic) pattern; (3) the network is evenly spread over the whole sheet, so the drainage density is fairly high; (4) most streams are drawn as solid lines and are therefore perennial, while the two broken lines in the north are seasonal; (5) a swamp covers the river floor in the south-east, which shows poor drainage and slow flow where the river reaches low ground. **Any four points carry full marks.**

items.enonce_markdown: On a fictitious sheet, the north-west quarter holds a nucleated town with a market, two schools, a hospital and a road junction. The south-east quarter has only three scattered farmsteads. In that quarter the contours are very close together and form a long escarpment, a large forest reserve is named, a broad swamp lies along the stream, and the only track ends at a footbridge. (a) With map evidence only, state two functions of the town (2 marks). (b) Give three reasons why settlement is scanty in the south-east quarter (3 marks). (c) Suggest one measure that would allow people to settle there (1 mark).
items.solution_markdown: (a) Commercial function (the market) and educational function (the two schools); health (the hospital) and transport (the road junction) are also acceptable. Any two with their symbol earn **2 marks**. (b) Award a mark for each of three evidenced reasons: the very closely spaced contours of the escarpment make the land steep and costly to build on; the named forest reserve restricts clearing and building; the swamp along the stream is waterlogged and prone to flooding; the lack of any road beyond the track that ends at a footbridge makes the area hard to reach. **Any three reasons carry full marks.** (c) Build an all-weather road with a bridge to link the quarter to the town, or drain the swamp edges and terrace the lower slopes. **One matching measure earns the mark.**

items_markdown: Every mark needs a point, map evidence (height, grid reference, name or symbol) and, when asked, the effect on people.
Close contours mean steep slopes; widely spaced contours mean gentle slopes; water flows from high to low ground.
Describe drainage by pattern, density, direction of flow, permanent or seasonal streams, and swamp or flood-prone ground.
Reasons for sparse settlement that a map supports: steep ground, swamp, reserve or forest, and lack of roads.
A measure must match the problem named: terracing and zigzag roads for slopes, drains, embankments and bridges for wet ground.
